reasoning_traces.think:
The ε-worst drop operator quantifies how much a tournament win probability degrades under small perturbations of matchup probabilities. It is defined as the difference between the true win probability and its infimum over all ε-perturbed matrices. This is computed using a multilinear decomposition wp = Σ α_ij·P_ij + β_ij, where α_ij captures sensitivity to P_ij. The key insight is that this diagnostic reveals which matchups most influence a team’s championship prospects. In GSE, this translates into identifying critical games whose outcome has maximal impact on futures positions. The operator is robust to noise in P_ij because it considers worst-case perturbations. However, it assumes deterministic brackets and does not account for stochasticity beyond the initial matchup model. Its failure mode occurs when the tournament structure deviates from balanced brackets or when estimation errors are not uniformly bounded.
